name: Ouagadougou Thomas Sankara International Airport
before:
Burkina Faso's only real air link. This one airport handles around 98 per cent of the country's scheduled commercial traffic, and Air Burkina and Air France between them carry about 60 per cent of the passengers.

It is remarkably close to town, roughly 1.5 km from the main commercial area, which makes for a fast transfer. That closeness is also the problem. The airport was built in the 1960s on what was then the southern edge of the city, and Ouagadougou has grown around it, so it now sits surrounded by development it has outgrown. The government has plans for a replacement 30 km to the north.

The site is long and narrow, about 4.8 km end to end, with a single 3,000 metre runway and a military sector alongside the civilian one.

Traffic grew steadily through the 2000s, passing 400,000 passengers in 2011.
after:
Ouagadougou's international airport, on the south east side of the city and close to the centre. It has a single 3,000 metre runway.

The FCDO advises against all travel to Burkina Faso.
